about: A loose angular boulder (talus block, field boulder): an irregular polyhedron of 6-9 oblique faces with a pair of off-parallel bedding faces, one or two corners broken off, thin partings, the top weathered rounder than the foot, a broad base sunk in the ground. Variants differ in proportion: a lump, a flat block, a tall wedge, a split block with a second leaning on it. Terrain kind `boulder`
place: on rock, under cliffs, shores; old terrain `boulder` rows are already sunk 0.12 x scale in z (lift them by that, or accept more buried)
